title: Quiet refactor sparring notebook — heuristics & micro-experiments
content:
Notes to self: quick, messy log of ideas to lower PR friction and validate small refactors. Not for wide circulation until I clean up.

Goal: reduce long review cycles caused by broad refactors; enable faster, lower-risk micro-steps. Capture techniques to 'spar' with reviewers — propose minimal surface changes that convey intent, carry tests, and leave clear rollback paths.

Top-level heuristics (short):
- One logical change per PR. If you must change 3 modules, split into 3 PRs with a short chore PR that wires the common interface (if needed).
- Always include a short "what not to worry about" section in the PR description when touching many files (call out formatting or rename-only changes).
- Prefer adding adapters/compat layers instead of in-place mass replacements. Adapter PR then follow-ups to remove shim.
- Add a short perf/backwards-compat note if behavior could affect latency or cache keys.

Micro-experiment log (small runs to test reviewer response):
1) tiny-adapter-pattern (2025-03-02) — PR: rename cache key helper -> shim+compat layer. Size: 12 changed files, 140 LOC (mostly renames). Outcome: +2 day review, blocker comments about naming; lesson: include before/after examples and automated find/replace script.
2) isolate-config-abstraction (2025-04-11) — PR: move config parsing to a new Config object + tests. Size: 4 files, 60 LOC. Outcome: accepted fast; reviewers liked focused tests and a changelog note.
3) batch-api-narrow (2025-06-07) — PR split: (A) add feature flag, (B) migrate one caller, (C) deprecate old path. Outcome: (A) review quick, (B) discussion about metrics, (C) deferred. Lesson: feature flag + metrics PR reduces risk but needs a dedicated metrics ticket.

Checklist to attach to PR description (copyable):
- Summary (1-2 lines): what changed and why.
- Scope: list of files and a phrase: "rename-only / adapter / logic change / perf tweak".
- Migration plan: steps to roll forward/back and expected user-visible changes.
- Tests included: unit / integration / canary plan.
- Metrics to watch (if applicable): latency P50/P95, error rate, cache hit.
- Rollback ETA and responsible oncall.
- Linked tickets and follow-ups.

Comment templates I keep using (short):
- For reviewers worried about behavior: "Helper preserves previous behavior; added a boolean flag to opt into new path — default = old behavior. See test X for case coverage."
- For reviewers suggesting large scope: "Agreed that broader cleanup is ideal. I split this work to keep the reviewable chunk small; follow-up ticket INF-XXXX created to address remaining items."

Small code snips I paste into PRs (inline):
- Quick adapter example:
  class NewFooAdapter:
      def __init__(self, old_impl):
          self._old = old_impl
      def decode(self, x):
          # preserves previous contract, will opt-in later
          return self._old.decode(x)

- Migration guard pattern: if os.getenv('ENABLE_X') == '1': use_new() else: use_old()

Sparring checklist for reviewers (what I'm asking for explicitly):
- Is the behavioral contract preserved? point to test(s) that prove it.
- Do names align with public API expectations? prefer conservative names.
- Any hidden perf regressions (KV cache, serialization hot paths)? flag and add micro-bench.
- Is the change reversible with a single revert? If not, add a rollback plan.

Open questions (need to resolve before next PR wave):
- Where to land short-lived adapters? new/internal/adapters/ feels noisy. Maybe: new/internal/shims/? Con: path proliferation.
- When is a rename-only PR too big? heuristic: >200 LOC across >10 files -> split.
- How do we communicate behavioral equivalence for nuanced cache keys? Add a one-off integration test harness?

Follow-ups (todo) — owners and quick status: 
- Create a tiny benchmark harness for KV serialization (owner: Ava) — JIRA INF-4410 — status: in_progress.
- Draft a tiny PR template snippet for "behavior preserved" section (owner: Morgan) — status: draft.
- Run a small internal signal: "two-week microrefactor challenge" to get reviewer feedback (owner: Ravi) — status: planning.

Signals to watch after merging micro-refactors:
- Latency P95 spike within first 24h. Quick rollback if >10% increase.
- Error rate + alerts on unusual exception types (deserializer errors).
- Increase in flakiness in integration tests referencing the changed module.

Random heuristics I've been experimenting with:
- Put the most controversial change in the first commit with an explicit test; keep subsequent commits purely mechanical. Reviewers can focus on first commit logic.
- Add a one-line human-readable summary at the top of large files for maintainers ("what this module does in 1 sentence"). It reduces review mental load.

Notes-to-self about conversation handling:
- If reviewer requests a big rename: propose a separate follow-up; explain why keep the PR small, offer the roadmap and link to follow-up ticket.
- If reviewer blocks for perf: run a 1-hour local micro-benchmark, paste numbers in the PR thread. Quick data beats speculation.

End-of-day quick log (today):
- Sketched adapter for config parsing, will open tiny PR with tests tomorrow.
- Pinged Ava about KV bench harness.
- Draft PR-snippet ready for reuse.

If I revisit later: collect 3 examples where small PRs reduced review time by >48h and make a short internal blurb for the eng newsletter.

-- morgan
